title: Remote Kv1.5 hyperpolarization suppresses tumor-like structures from two oncogenes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Remote Kv1.5 hyperpolarization suppresses tumor-like structures from two oncogenes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In Xenopus laevis embryos, misexpressing the hyperpolarizing potassium channel Kv1.5 in a blastomere distant from the oncogene-injected blastomere reduces the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 35% for Xrel3 and about 29% for Gli1, indicating the suppression is not specific to one oncogene.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Kv1.5-induced long-distance hyperpolarization was also able to significantly suppress Xrel3 and Gli1 ITLS formation by 34.9% (N=225; t-test, P<0.05) and 29.4% (N=292; t-test, P<0.05), respectively (Fig. 2C), suggesting the effect is not specific for just one type of oncogene.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS”. Scope: 16-cell-stage Xenopus laevis embryos co-injected with Xrel3 or Gli1 and Kv1.5 mRNA in separate blastomeres, scored at stage 34

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The outcomes, sample sizes, and decision criterion are explicit and readily analyzed. The public record supports a limited audit, but not a fully independent reanalysis or a broad claim across oncogenes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute tumor-like-structure incidence and effect sizes for Xrel3 and Gli1 embryos with remote Kv1.5 expression versus oncogene-only controls. Suppression for both oncogenes near the reported magnitudes supports non-specificity to one oncogene.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Only two oncogene classes are tested in this contrast.

Complete contingency tables and individual embryo records are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data existence: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.98

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The two effect sizes, sample sizes, and significance calls are published measurements of a clearly defined contrast. They can be checked for the stated direction and for consistency across Xrel3 and Gli1. Without embryo-level data, injection failures and the voltage of the distant site cannot be re-audited, so the result is only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare induced-tumor incidence at stage 34 for Xrel3 and for Gli1 with and without Kv1.5 mRNA in a distant blastomere. Reductions near the reported 35% and 29%, with voltage changed only at the remote site, would support the result; no reduction for either oncogene would refute non-specificity across these two drivers.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A t-test on incidence proportions is a weak summary, and remote voltage was not archived animal by animal.

Raw embryo scores underlying the percentages are not public.
